# Exact projective continuation costs on a genuinely nonaffine critical triple

This is an actual three-fiber calibration of the new continuation, not a
general payment theorem. The smaller-endpoint choice pays every original
critical cap. The larger-endpoint choice fails that test. The old symmetric
perspective has mixed fixed-cap signs but POSITIVE response-weighted
payment, so this example does not refute its reoptimized first variation.

## 1. Actual bodies, source, and certified critical caps

Use the all-direction globally critical example proved in
`candidate c0a17a15efbe8efa`:

    h=20/97, t=100/291, e0=1/100,
    K_r={x,y>=0, h<=x+y<=r},
    A=K_(1-e0), K=K_1, B=K_(1+e0).

These are the ONLY three fibers, at integer bases -1,0,1. They satisfy
K=(A+B)/2. Write a=1-e0 and b=1+e0. The actual globally deepest source is
Y=(0,t,t), with raw depth Q and total mass M:

    Q=18200/28227,
    M=135144409/94090000,
    beta=Q/M=182000000/405433227.                         (1)

Put s=3t-1. Three actual globally critical caps through Y are

    H1: x+y<=2t,
    H2: t*x+s*y-e0*t*z>=t(4t-1),
    H3: s*x+t*y-e0*t*z>=t(4t-1).                         (2)

Their middle traces cover the entire middle plane. Every endpoint fiber
has area strictly below Q and is isolated by a closed integer halfspace.
These are full-normal, actual global claims from the cited exact proof,
not inferences from the three-cap display alone.

This is genuinely outside affine centroid graphs. Each coordinate of the
centroid of K_r equals

    g(r)=r/3+h^2/[3(r+h)],
    g''(r)=2h^2/[3(r+h)^3]>0.                            (3)

Thus the midpoint of the endpoint centroids is different from the middle
centroid. The chosen deepest source need not equal any ordinary centroid.

The source coarea lengths for H1,H2,H3 are 2t,2,2 in the displayed normal
normalizations, and the full three-fiber lengths are three times these.
The positive continuous-normal relation has coefficients (4t-1,1,1).
Consequently the actual response weights are

    theta1=109/309, theta2=theta3=100/309.                 (4)

They are used below only to distinguish the rowwise and weighted tests.

## 2. An exact algebraic projective-centroid parameter

By symmetry the projective parameter relative to y=(t,t) has equal
coordinates (c,c). Put u=x+y. The transformed centroid is zero precisely
when

    integral_h^1 u(u-2t)/[1+c(u-2t)]^4 du=0.             (5)

The two coordinate equations agree by symmetry; their sum is (5).
Direct rational integration gives

    (5)'s integral =
      -29644461(509600c^2-1777040c+28227)
       /[(91c+291)^3(140c-291)^3].                       (6)

The admissible root is

    c=(44426-1067 sqrt(1702))/25480,
    15957301/10^9 < c < 15957302/10^9.                   (7)

The denominator 1+c(u-2t) is positive on the whole original K. The other
quadratic root exceeds 291/140 and is inadmissible at u=h. Thus (7) is the
actual projective-centroid normalization, not a chosen approximate field.

Define the two functions used by the boundary integrals:

    f(u)=[1+c(u-2t)]^(-2),
    g(u)=[1+c((u+h)/2-2t)]^(-2).                         (8)

In the globally finite projective field these are restrictions of the
inverse-square function with its positive convex tangent extension below
its minimum denominator on K. None of the evaluations below uses that
extension: all its arguments are at least the minimum at u=h.

For any l<=r in the occurring ranges the exact integrals are

    I(l,r)=integral_l^r f(u)du
           =(r-l)/[(1+c(l-2t))(1+c(r-2t))],
    J(l,r)=integral_l^r g(u)du
           =(r-l)/[(1+c((l+h)/2-2t))
                    (1+c((r+h)/2-2t))].                (9)

## 3. All actual costs from the four physical facets

Choose the old perspective centers y_A=y_B=y. This is permitted since y
is interior to both endpoints. On the two coordinate facets its field
is t*f(u). On the inner diagonal its field times arclength contributes
h(2t-h)f(h). On the outer diagonal of K_r it contributes
r(r-2t)f(1): the support ratio in the argument cancels r-2t exactly.
Therefore its actual total first cost and fixed-cap losses on K_r are

    D(r)=2t I(h,r)+h(2t-h)f(h)+r(r-2t)f(1),
    L1(r)=2t I(h,2t)+h(2t-h)f(h),
    L2(r)=t I(r-2+4t,r)+2t(r-2t)f(1).                   (10)

H3 has the same loss as H2. These formulas retain the ACTUAL ambient
integer tilts in(2): its relevant coordinate-facet threshold is r-2+4t,
and its outer diagonal portion has coordinate length exactly 2t.

For the new one-input construction, an a-minimizing partner is any point
of the other fiber's inner diagonal u=h. The selected input has field
2H(n)g(u), where H is the middle support distance from y. Thus its total
cost and two distinct fixed-cap losses are

    DO(r)=4t J(h,r)+2h(2t-h)g(h)+2r(1-2t)g(r),
    O1(r)=4t J(h,2t)+2h(2t-h)g(h),
    O2(r)=2t J(r-2+4t,r)+4t(1-2t)g(r).                 (11)

These are surface integrals of the actual fields. No cap centroid or
independent cap-wise allocation is substituted for the same deformation.
All the displayed cuts are proper, so facet/cut crossings have arclength
zero and cause no boundary-mass ambiguity in the first variation.

For each of three paths form its total cost and losses by

    old:  Dtot=D(a)+D(1)+D(b), Ljtot=Lj(a)+Lj(1)+Lj(b),
    oneA: Dtot=D(1)+DO(a),      Ljtot=Lj(1)+Oj(a),
    oneB: Dtot=D(1)+DO(b),      Ljtot=Lj(1)+Oj(b).         (12)

Put Pj=Ljtot-beta*Dtot and Pbar=theta1*P1+2theta2*P2.
The following rational bounds hold EXACTLY at the algebraic parameter(7):

| path | P1 | P2=P3 | weighted Pbar |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| old | >12/1000 | <-6/1000 | >3/10000 |
| oneA | >17/1000 | >49/10000 | >9/1000 |
| oneB | <-1/2000 | <-13/1000 | <-8/1000 |

An exact rational-interval certificate is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_nonaffine_projective_one_input_payment_defect_transport.py`.
It verifies the signs of the quadratic at both endpoints in(7), its
strictly negative derivative there, and performs interval arithmetic on
the explicit rational functions(9)--(12). Every denominator is checked
positive. Hence the table is an exact algebraic sign certificate; printed
decimal interval displays are not used as evidence. It also verifies(6),
the centroid formula, all facet/cap status ranges, and the original-mass
normalization. The current run passes79 exact checks.

## 4. What the payment proves, and what it does not

The oneA fields and the unchanged B satisfy exact midpoint compatibility
by the proved one-input construction. The middle uses its actual gauge
erosion, and all changed fibers remain nested convex bodies. Every fixed
cap in(2) loses more than beta times the SAME total loss, with minimum
strict excess49/10000. Their middle-plane cover persists unchanged.
The endpoint isolation caps retain their strict mass gap. For all small
positive erosion parameters e, the induced convex-hull family therefore
has actual global normalized depth at most

    beta - [49/(10000 M)] e + o(e) < beta.               (13)

No regular response theorem or movement of the critical normals is
needed for this conclusion: it uses fixed closed covers and their actual
first losses. The new family still has exactly the three integer fibers.

The larger-endpoint oneB choice fails this entire fixed-menu first-order
test. That alone is not a proof that its actual global depth cannot
decrease, since other cap menus may become active. Likewise the old path
fails to pay each fixed row, but its weighted payment is positive; this
note expressly does NOT call it a reoptimized-response obstruction.

The calculation establishes a genuine nonaffine instance where choosing
the input charged by the continuation matters, and where the smaller
input supplies a fixed-cover global descent. This example was already
above the OC target. No automatic payment for arbitrary triples or
arbitrary integer bases follows.
